sentences.text: The petition under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (in short 'Cr.P.C.') has been preferred by the petitioners for quashment of FIR registered at Crime No.7/2022 at Police Station Madhav Nagar, Ujjain for offences under Sections 420, 467 and 468 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in Short 'IPC').
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: The facts of the case briefly state are that petitioner No.1 Manoj Khandelwal prepared a forged will dated 21.02.2021 of complainant's husband late Harihar Kumar and submitted the same in the Municipal Corporation, Ujjain for transferring his house bearing No.38, Dashhara Maidan, Ujjain.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is alleged against the petitioner No.2 Manish alongwith petitioner No.3 Ravindra assisted the petitioner No.1 Manoj in the aforesaid crime and signed on the above forged will as witness and submitted their affidavit in support of the same before the Municipal Corporation, Ujjain.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: After completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed, but case is not committed to the Sessions Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: Subsequently, on the basis of the amicable settlement arrived at between the petitioners and the complainant, a joint compromise petition under Section 320(2) of Cr.P.C. was filed before this Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: On verification, Principal Registrar has certified on 19.01.2022 that both the parties have entered into a compromise without any threat, inducement and coercion from either side and they have voluntarily entered into compromise.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is submitted by counsel for the petitioners that the matter pertains to offence registered against the petitioner under Sections 420, 467 and 468 of IPC has been amicably settled between both the parties and complainant has no more grievance against the petitioner.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: Therefore, continuance of proceedings before the trial Court will amount to sheer wastage of valuable time of the Court and will also result in harassment of the parties.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is also submitted that in the same offence co- accused Manu Sharma has filed an application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashment of FIR on the basis of the amicable settlement same was allowed vide order dated 23.06.2022 passed in MCRC No.26888/2022.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: FIR and further proceedings of the Sessions trial has been quashed in respect of the co- accused Manu Sharma.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: The Hon'ble apex Court in the case of Central Bureau of Investigation vs. Sadhu Ram Singh & Ors., (2017) 5 SCC 350, while considering the exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 and 320 of Cr.P.C., has upheld the quashment of non- compoundable offences, pursuant to settlement arrived at by the parties, holding that exercise of judicial restraint vis- -vis continuance of criminal proceedings after compromise arrived at between the parties, may amount to abuse of process of Court and futile exercise.

entities.text: Central Bureau of Investigation vs. Sadhu Ram Singh & Ors., (2017) 5 SCC 350
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: Taking into account the law laid down by Hon'ble apex Court, in the opinion of this Court, as the compromise between the parties was arrived at between the parties, thus continuation of the prosecution in such matters will be a futile exercise, which will serve no purpose.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: Under such a situation, Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. can be justifiably invoked to prevent abuse of process of law and wasteful exercise by the Courts below.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: More so, offence in question are not against the society, but merely affect the victim.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has placed reliance upon a judgment delivered by the apex Court in the case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and Anr.

sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: reported in 2012 Cr.L.R. (SC) 883 .

sentences.text: Paragraph nos.49, 52, 53 and 57 of the aforesaid judgments
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text:
are reads as under:-
'49.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: Section 482 of the Code, as its very language suggests, saves the inherent power of the High Court which it has by virtue of it being a superior court to prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: It begins with the words, 'nothing in this Code' which means that the provision is an overriding provision.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: These words leave no manner of doubt that none of the provisions of the Code limits or restricts the inherent power.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: The guideline for exercise of such power is provided in Section 482 itself i.e., to prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: As has been repeatedly stated that Section 482 confers no new powers on High Court; it merely safeguards existing inherent powers possessed by High Court necessary to prevent abuse of the process of any Court or to secure the ends of justice.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is equally well settled that the power is not to be resorted to if there is specific provision in the Code for the redress of the grievance of an aggrieved party.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text:
It should be exercised very sparingly and it should not be exercised as against the express bar of law engrafted in any other provision of the Code.
52.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: It needs no emphasis that exercise of inherent power by the High Court would entirely depend on the facts and circumstances of each case.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is neither permissible nor proper for the court to provide a straitjacket formula regulating the exercise of inherent powers under Section 482.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: No precise and inflexible 6 guidelines can also be provided.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: 53. Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings on the ground of settlement between an offender and victim is not the same thing as compounding of offence.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: They are different and not interchangeable.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: Strictly speaking, the power of compounding of offences given to a court under Section 320 is materially different from the quashing of criminal proceedings by the High Court in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: In compounding of offences, power of a criminal court is circumscribed by the provisions contained in Section 320 and the court is guided solely and squarely thereby while, on the other hand, the formation of opinion by the High Court for quashing a criminal offence or criminal proceeding or criminal complaint is guided by the material on record as to whether the ends of justice would justify such exercise of power although the ultimate consequence may be acquittal or dismissal of indictment.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: 57.The position that emerges from the above discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation but it has to be exercised in Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168077537/
3 accord with the guideline engrafted in such power viz; (i) to secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.

entities.text: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: In what cases power to quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R may be exercised where the offender and victim have settled their dispute would depend on the facts and circumstances of each case and no category can be prescribed.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text:
However, before exercise of such power,
the High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc.
cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victims family and the offender have settled the dispute.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: Such offences are not private in nature and have serious impact on society.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: Similarly, any compromise between the victim and offender in relation to the offences under special statutes like Prevention of corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants while working in that capacity etc; cannot provide for any basis for quashing criminal proceedings involving such offences.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text:
But the criminal cases having overwhelmingly and pre-dominatingly civil flavour stand on different footing for the purposes of quashing, particularly the offences arising from commercial, financial, mercantile,
civil, partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, etc. or the family disputes where the wrong is basically private or personal in nature and the parties have resolved their entire dispute.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: In this category of cases, High Court may quash criminal proceedings if in its view, because of the compromise between the offender and victim, the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak and continuation of criminal case would put accused to great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal case despite full and complete settlement and compromise with the victim.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of the criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding.'
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: Keeping in view the aforesaid judgments and also keeping in view the fact that parties have arrived at amicable settlement, looking to the dictum of the apex Court in the case of Sadhu Ram Singh (Supra) and Gian Singh (Supra), it would be in the interest of justice to quash the proceedings in respect of Crime No.7/2022.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the petition is hereby allowed and the First Information Report in Crime No.7/2022,
Police Station Madhav Nagar, Ujjain, against the petitioners for offences under Section 420, 467 and 468 of the IPC as well as the consequent proceedings pending before the trial Court are hereby quashed.

It is equally well settled that the power is not to be resorted to if there is specific provision in the Code for the redress of the grievance of an aggrieved party.
It should be exercised very sparingly and it should not be exercised as against the express bar of law engrafted in any other provision of the Code.
52.
It is neither permissible nor proper for the court to provide a straitjacket formula regulating the exercise of inherent powers under Section 482.
Strictly speaking, the power of compounding of offences given to a court under Section 320 is materially different from the quashing of criminal proceedings by the High Court in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction.
In compounding of offences, power of a criminal court is circumscribed by the provisions contained in Section 320 and the court is guided solely and squarely thereby while, on the other hand, the formation of opinion by the High Court for quashing a criminal offence or criminal proceeding or criminal complaint is guided by the material on record as to whether the ends of justice would justify such exercise of power although the ultimate consequence may be acquittal or dismissal of indictment.
Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation but it has to be exercised in Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168077537/
3 accord with the guideline engrafted in such power viz; (i) to secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.
In what cases power to quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R may be exercised where the offender and victim have settled their dispute would depend on the facts and circumstances of each case and no category can be prescribed.
However, before exercise of such power,
the High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime.
Heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc.
cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victims family and the offender have settled the dispute.
Such offences are not private in nature and have serious impact on society.
Similarly, any compromise between the victim and offender in relation to the offences under special statutes like Prevention of corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants while working in that capacity etc; cannot provide for any basis for quashing criminal proceedings involving such offences.
But the criminal cases having overwhelmingly and pre-dominatingly civil flavour stand on different footing for the purposes of quashing, particularly the offences arising from commercial, financial, mercantile,
civil, partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, etc. or the family disputes where the wrong is basically private or personal in nature and the parties have resolved their entire dispute.
In this category of cases, High Court may quash criminal proceedings if in its view, because of the compromise between the offender and victim, the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak and continuation of criminal case would put accused to great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal case despite full and complete settlement and compromise with the victim.

opennyai_summary.21_June_2023__facts:
This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 o f Cr.P.C., as he is implicated in connection with FIR/Crime No.145/2020 registered at Police Station Malhargarh,
District Mandsaur (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 406, 409, 34 of IPC and Sections 3, 4, 5 and 6 of the Prize Chits and Money Circulation Scheme (Banning) Act and Section 6(1) of M.P. Nikshepakon Ke Hiton Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam.
As per prosecution case, the main accused Fayaz Khan induced the complainant to invest in the Bit Coin trade alluring and assuring him huge profits.
He charged a total of Rs.62,000/- in three parts (24,000/- + 24,000/- + 14,000/-) under the pretext of making his ID to transact in the trade,
but later refused to return the same stating that the company, with whom he was dealing with has closed down their shutters and has disappeared.
Thereafter, an FIR was lodged against the main accused Fayaz Khan.
During Investigation, the present applicant is implicated in the case on the basis of memorandum statement of Fayaz Khan which was recorded under Section 27 of the Evidence Act.
opennyai_summary.21_June_2023__arguments:
The applicant is innocent and has not committed the offence and he has been falsely implicated in the case.
04. Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer and submits that the applicant has a criminal past.
Therefore, he is not entitled to get bail.
opennyai_summary.21_June_2023__decision:
The trial will take sufficient long time for its disposal, on this ground prayer is made to enlarged the applicant on bail.
06. Considering the facts and circumstances coupled with the fact that final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, the application is allowed.
07. The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand) with two solvent sureties out of which one shall be local surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his/her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he / she shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
2] This is the first application filed by the applica Section 482 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/Section 438 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail as they are apprehending their arrest in connection with Crime No.55/2022 registered at Police Station Maheshwar, District Khargone for the offence punishable under Sections 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 4, 6(1) of M.P.
Nikshepako ke Hito ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam, 2000. 3] Allegation against the applicants is that they were also involved in the aforesaid case of fraud of Rs.21,75,656/-
4] Counsel for the applicants has submitted that the main accused in the present case is Bhupendra Teli, who is still absconding, who was the President of the AU Co- operative Society and had appointed the office bearers in fifty-five places, and the applicants were the Vice President and Director of the society respectively.
Counsel has submitted that the applicants have not signed any document and the amount received from the investors has been credited in the account of the Society only, and the applicants were not given any amount by the complainants in their accounts,
and there are no criminal antecedents.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
6] Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the case diary as Manoj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23296454/
1 also the statements of various complainants, this Court finds that the main allegations are against co-accused Bhupendra Teli, who was the President of the Society at Branch Maheshwar, and the amount has been deposited in the account of the Society only, and there is nothing on record to suggest that any amount was received directly by the applicants in their account.
In such circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that the custodial interrogation of the applicants, against whom there are no criminal antecedents, would not be necessary.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
7] Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.
It is directed that in the event of arrest, applicants shall be released on bail, upon their executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand only)each and furnishing separate solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
The applicants shall make themselves available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.
They shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
8] Accordingly, MCRC stands allowed and disposed of.
